persona_summary: CS 5th-year, Tech Entrepreneurship minor, 41 courses, Good standing
question: I need to take 3 courses this summer to graduate on time. My job offer starts in September so I need to be done by August. Plan my summer schedule.
false_assumption_or_hidden_conflict: Summer sessions typically have unit/course limits that are lower than regular semesters. Taking 3 courses in summer may exceed the summer unit cap. Additionally, not all courses are offered in summer, and summer sessions may be shorter, meaning course availability is limited.
naive_system_response: A naive system schedules 3 courses in summer without checking summer-specific unit limits or course availability, producing a plan that may not be possible.
correct_response: Summer sessions at CMU-Q have a unit limit of [X] units. Three courses would total approximately [Y] units. If this exceeds the limit, you can take a maximum of [N] courses in summer. Additionally, check which of your remaining courses are actually offered in summer — options are typically limited. Here's a feasible plan: [summer courses] + [remaining courses in a different term if needed].
why_multi_agent_helps: The Policy Agent catches the summer unit limit. The Courses Agent checks which courses are offered in summer sessions. A single agent might assume summer works like a regular semester and build an infeasible plan.
key_facts: Summer sessions have different unit limits than regular semesters
Not all courses are offered in summer
Summer sessions may have shorter duration affecting scheduling
Job start date creates a hard deadline
known_traps: Treating summer like a regular semester for planning purposes
Scheduling courses that aren't offered in summer
advisor_validation_needed: Verify: (1) summer unit cap from policy data, (2) summer 2026 course offerings, (3) whether 3 summer courses is permitted, (4) P-010's exact remaining requirements
